units.title: A gradient-query interpreter that counts the successful test
units.boundary: Exact-real noncomputable finite-fuel semantics, not floating-point software. This definition alone proves neither termination nor accuracy. It records output and count, not a query-list trace.

sources.label: Chen–Chewi–Lu–Zhang, SPHMC Algorithm D.2
sources.scope: Attributed paraphrase; Samplinglib's finite-fuel representation is explicit implementation structure.

assumptions: E is a real normed vector space. g:E→E is an arbitrary oracle, eta and eps are real parameters, y is the fixed center, x is the current point, and fuel is a natural number. No regularity or positivity is required just to define the interpreter.
units.statement: With no fuel return none. Otherwise evaluate g at x, form z=y−eta g(x), and test the residual. Success returns the current x and count one. Failure recurses at z with one less fuel and adds one to a successful returned count; unsuccessful recursion returns none.

steps.title: Spend one query before testing
steps.text: Even an immediately successful residual test needs the gradient at the current point. The let-bound z represents that single oracle evaluation. Mathematical arithmetic and comparison are exact; this is not a numerical-roundoff model.
steps.lean: The positive-fuel branch binds z before the if; success is some (x,1).

steps.title: Return the tested point, not the next point
steps.text: The certificate in the companion theorem controls the error at x through the residual between x and z. Therefore the successful branch returns x. Each unsuccessful level contributes exactly one additional query to the recursively returned count.
steps.lean: Option.map preserves failure and increments only the count in a successful pair; run_first_stop proves the recurrence's execution equation.

units.lean_statement: The adjacent disclosure extracts the exact oracle, real parameters, natural fuel, and Option-valued return type from Lean.
units.lean_proof: This is a recursive definition, not an independently proved accuracy theorem. Its execution is certified by approximate_proximal_execution.

units.title: Measurable stopped proximal execution with certified pointwise work
units.boundary: Algorithm D.2/Lemma D.3 only. No expected cost along a sampler, Picard moment bound, D.1 stability bound, sampling convergence or full SPHMC result is proved here. Independent encoder-denoiser publication admission is pending.

sources.label: Fan Chen, Sinho Chewi, Jianfeng Lu and Matthew S. Zhang, SPHMC D.2–D.3
sources.scope: Faithful attributed restatement with Samplinglib-derived measurability, quantitative unique minimum, exact interpreter semantics and explicit admissible constant.

assumptions: E is a finite-dimensional complete real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure. This includes Euclidean space and dimension zero.

V:E→R is C², kappa≥1, and for every x,v its genuine second derivative satisfies kappa⁻¹‖v‖²≤D²V(x)[v,v]≤‖v‖². ContDiff makes the displayed fderiv a genuine derivative, not merely a totalized expression.
Fix 0<eta≤c<1 and eps>0. The constant c is uniform in the center y. No restriction eta≤1/2 is imposed. There is no assumed approximate proximal oracle and no assumed measurability of the output.
units.statement: There exist measurable maps p:E→E and N:E→N. For each y, p(y) is the unique minimizer of F_y(x)=V(x)+‖x−y‖²/(2eta). Starting at y and iterating T_y(x)=y−eta∇V(x), N(y) is the first residual test success. The measurable returned point x_N is eps-close to p(y); the exact interpreter succeeds with fuel N(y)+1, returning that point and count N(y)+1, bounded by C_c[1+log(1+‖∇V(y)‖/eps)].

steps.title: Curvature gives a strict contraction
steps.text: The canonical quadratic-regularization lemma at zero regularization gives a 1-Lipschitz gradient and strong convexity of V. Subtracting two images under T_y cancels the center, so multiplication by eta gives a strict contraction. Completeness then supplies its unique fixed point p(y).
steps.lean: QuadraticRegularization supplies hg; stopped_contraction constructs ContractingWith and its fixedPoint.

steps.title: Identify a genuine unique proximal minimum
steps.text: The canonical first-order regularization formula shows that the fixed point has zero gradient for F_y. Its strong-convexity modulus is kappa inverse plus eta inverse. Applying the first-order lower bound at that point gives quantitative quadratic growth. Its strictly positive coefficient forces any other minimizer to coincide with p(y).
steps.lean: curvature_gradient_and_smoothness proves the gradient identity; firstOrder_lower_bound_of_strongConvexOn proves growth, then positivity proves uniqueness.

steps.title: Produce a finite stopping certificate
steps.text: Successive residuals decay geometrically. Put z=‖∇V(y)‖ and t=(1−c)eps, both with t strictly positive. Taking the natural ceiling B below gives c^B≤1/(1+z/t), hence z c^B≤t. Since eta≤c and eta<1, the actual residual at B is no larger than t and therefore passes the test. This establishes existence before selecting a first index.
steps.formula: \begin{gathered}\|x_{n+1}-x_n\|\le\eta^{n+1}\|\nabla V(y)\|,\\ B=\left\lceil\frac{\log(1+z/t)}{-\log c}\right\rceil,\quad zc^B\le t\le(1-\eta)\varepsilon,\quad N\le B.\end{gathered}
steps.lean: dist_iterate_succ_le_geometric and geometric_certificate prove hcert; Nat.find_spec/min/min' give success, first-hit minimality and the bound.

steps.title: Explain the measurability that a sampler needs
steps.text: Every iterate is measurable as a function of y by induction and continuity of the gradient. Their pointwise limit is p(y), hence measurable. Each residual-test set is Borel. The least successful index is measurable, and selecting the N(y)-th member of this countable measurable family yields a measurable returned point. No integration or exchange of integrals is used.
steps.lean: measurable_of_tendsto_metrizable, measurable_find and Measurable.find discharge limit, index and selected-output measurability.

steps.title: Convert the residual to actual distance
steps.text: The contraction posterior-error estimate bounds the current iterate's distance to the fixed point by its residual divided by 1−eta. The denominator is strictly positive. At the selected first hit the test is exactly strong enough to bound this quotient by eps.
steps.lean: ContractingWith.aposteriori_dist_iterate_fixedPoint_le followed by div_le_iff₀; the bound concerns x_N, not x_(N+1).

steps.title: Bound the number of real oracle queries
steps.text: The ceiling estimate first gives N+1≤2+log(1+z/((1−c)eps))/(-log c). For R=z/eps, use 1+R/(1−c)≤(1+R)/(1−c), then log monotonicity. The displayed C_c dominates the resulting affine expression in log(1+R). It is an explicit Samplinglib choice, not a constant printed in the source; it depends only on c. When the initial gradient vanishes, one query is still required.
steps.lean: count_bound uses Nat.ceil_lt_add_one and Real.log_div; positivity uses 0<c<1 and R≥0.

steps.title: Tie the proof to the actual interpreter
steps.text: All tests before N fail and the test at N succeeds. Induction over these failed tests unfolds one interpreter step at a time. The final step returns the current point with one query; unwinding increments the count to N+1. This is a pointwise evaluation theorem, not a theorem about expectations for randomly generated centers.
steps.lean: run_first_stop proves the recurrence equation; focused tests exercise returned point, count, insufficient fuel and eta=3/4.
